Revolutionary War.xlsx, Cowpens: the light infantry, Legion infantry, 7th and 71st (CP56, CP66, CP76, CP104) are drawn until 07:56, a few minutes after they laid down their arms, not 08:30; Washington's pursuit (CP37) is drawn arriving at 08:22, not 08:16, so he stays behind Tarleton; settings follow.hold_until, follow.glide_rate, follow.glide_seconds, lead.until, texts.after and texts.lost. What changed on 24 November 2026 (evening): the Cowpens playback after Morgan's review

Revolutionary War.xlsx, Cowpens: the page opens on the whole ground and eases in; units outside the current event keep 70% of their strength; Tarleton's column marches as one symbol (C-BR-TARL, rows CP40 and a new row CP138) and its eight units set off from CP138 instead of marching the road on top of one another; arrows reach 6 minutes ahead; rows that meet blend over 4 minutes. No source reading changed. With player fixes for two jumps (a move along a route that began away from the unit, and the end of a route into a line) and eased event dimming. What changed on 24 November 2026 (later still): Tarleton's road at Cowpens

Revolutionary War.xlsx: at Morgan's request, routes RC01 to RC06 (Tarleton's march in, the British escapes, Washington's pursuit) leave the straight line across the 900 m between today's Green River Road and the old trace, and follow the road the maps show there: north on a road of the 1959 USGS sheet (S108) that Landers (1928, S103) calls "Green River Road", then west on Bearss's Mill Gap road (S107). CP40 moves about 1 km up the road so it stays 3.3 km by road from the field. Gap CG06 partly closed. Written by pipeline/cowpens_tarleton_road_2026_11_24.py.
What changed on 24 November 2026 (later): a reconstructed 1781 map of the Cowpens, and nine other maps of the ground

Revolutionary War.xlsx, Cowpens only: a WarMapper reconstruction of the ground in January 1781 (Reconstructions, Recon layers; data/recon/cowpens-1781.geojson), on today's terrain, is the base the playback opens on. Nine other maps are fitted to the ground and offered under "Other maps of this ground": Bearss's four plates of 1967 (one base that follows the clock), Landers's two sketches of 1928, the USGS sheets of 1959 and 1975, Mills's map of 1825 and the park map. New sources S108 to S111; S107 may be hosted. Gap CG02 closed; a note on CG06. Written by pipeline/cowpens_period_maps_2026_11_24.py.
What changed on 24 November 2026: Cowpens after its audit

Revolutionary War.xlsx, Cowpens only: the 90 position rows were audited against their sources, and Bearss's 1967 study was read (new source S107). Five rows marked `stated` became `inferred` and eight `medium` ratings became `low`; three `medium` rows remain (CP20, CP24, CP32). The British first line moved back 155 m (CH16), the British surrender back 95 m, Morgan's camp to the ravine Bearss draws, and Washington's charge to behind the British right. Every page cited from S103 and S104 moved up one (both books print page numbers at the foot), with five fixes to S95 pages. New hypotheses CH16 and CH17; Bearss added to seven others; gap CG01 closed. Written by pipeline/cowpens_audit_2026_11_24.py.
What changed on 23 November 2026 (evening): the Battle of Cowpens

Revolutionary War.xlsx: a second campaign (ARW-SOU, Greene's campaign in the Carolinas) and its first battle, Cowpens, 17 January 1781 (playback "cowpens"): 31 units, 90 position rows (CP01 to CP137), 11 routes, 14 events, 15 hypotheses (CH01 to CH15) and 8 gaps (CG01 to CG08). Sources S95 to S106 are new here: the Army's 1996 staff ride handbook and the eyewitness documents it prints, the Army War College study of 1928, the National Park Service handbook, and the park's waysides. Two candidates added (SC-SOU08, SC-SOU09). Every position is placed by a distance the sources give, measured along the Green River Road on today's map (pipeline/cowpens_geo.py); none is rated above medium. Not read: Bearss (1967), Ward, Babits. Written by pipeline/cowpens_2026_11_23.py. The exporter now reads one new kind of setting, sides.<code>.short and sides.<code>.name, so a playback can name a side for itself (the Crown side is "Hessian and British" for Trenton and "British" here); no battle file format change.
What changed on 23 November 2026: the workbook is split by war

The battle data is now one workbook per war (Revolutionary War, U.S. Civil War, Philippine War, World War I) and this one, Sources and notes, in the folder data/WarMapper battle data/. Each war's workbook has the same sheets in the same order and holds only that war's rows. This file holds what every war shares: this change log, Sources and Source candidates (one register, so an S-id is never used twice), and the two gaps that belong to no one war. No id changed, and every battle file is written exactly as before. export_battles.py reads all five files, and writes each sheet as a CSV file under csv/ so a change shows line by line on GitHub.
What changed on 23 November 2026 (later): Hypotheses in place of Conflicts

Each war's workbook has a Hypotheses sheet in place of Conflicts: one row per disputed point, with the competing readings, the evidence for and against the adopted one (source and page), the adopted reading, its confidence, who decided and when. All 59 Conflicts rows are carried over under their own ids, with their old text in a history column. New evidence: Calef, Buford, Gamble, Wadsworth and Dawes (Official Records, vol. 27, pt. 1, S62) and the German account of Ypres (S41) with page numbers. Elliott (S59) was checked page by page: five Trenton citations of 17 Nov were one page early (pp. 41, 46, 47, 48 should be 42, 47, 48, 49); the Hypotheses give the right pages. The same slip may be in the Positions rows that cite S59 (see Gaps).

What changed on 21 November 2026 (later): a reconstructed base map for Manila

Two new sheets. Reconstructions: one row per reconstructed base map (a map drawn by the page from traced lines, in period dress; always labelled a reconstruction). Recon layers: one row per layer of it, with its source, method (traced, AI-extracted, interpolated), confidence, dates and a link to the original map. The lines themselves are in data/recon/<id>.geojson, where every feature repeats its own source, method, confidence and dates; tools/export_battles.py puts both into the battle file. A base is switched on with Playback settings bases.N.recon.

Manila: new source S78 (Haan's engineer map of February 1899, National Archives); six source candidates (SC-PW11 to SC-PW16); 53 Labels rows with show = recon (names as lettered on S78, drawn on the reconstructed base only). No position row was changed. The engineer map puts blockhouses 5 to 7 and the San Juan bridge about 300 m east of where the Signal Corps map's fit (S64) put them, and today's river agrees with the engineer map: positions read from S64 in that sector need a second look.
Three battles in one linked set of tables: the first day at Gettysburg (1 July 1863), Trenton (25-26 December 1776) and First Ypres (18 October to 22 November 1914). Built 12 Nov 2026.
What changed on 18 November 2026 (route check): Birmingham at 6 a.m.; Greene's road by Parkway Avenue

Checked against the Washington Crossing Park Association's driving tour (new source S63). The army now reaches Birmingham at about 06:00 (T04; event TE05), two hours after the march began, as Elliott (S59) and the tour have it, and Jacobs Creek at about 05:10 (T03). Greene's road (RT03) now follows today's Upper Ferry Road and Parkway Avenue to Pennington Road, as the tour gives it, in place of a loop up Scotch Road and a straight guess; it passes the south end of today's Scotch Road. Sullivan's road already matched the tour (Bear Tavern Road, Grand Avenue, Sullivan Way, West State Street). See TC02 (v11 column) and TG02.
What changed on 18 November 2026 (later): Trenton crossing, escapes, routes taken and the 1777 map

Crossing (revised the same day at Morgan's request): Trenton opens at 18:00 on 25 December. The army crosses as one symbol (T00 to T01) and divides on the New Jersey bank into Greene's and Sullivan's divisions; they and Knox's artillery (new unit T-US-KNOX, with Forrest, Hamilton and Bauman under him) are drawn whole until the first shots (playback settings formations.until and formations.also). 'Crossing the Delaware' (TE01) is now named on the timeline. All times on the maps and timeline are 24-hour.

Escapes: the British dragoons now ride to Princeton (T62, route RT12), the jägers go to Bordentown (T63, RT13; see TC18), and a new unit, the men of the Knyphausen regiment who forded the Assunpink (T-HE-KNYPX, T64 and T65, RT14), makes for Crosswicks. The playback runs to 11:30. New event TE16. The new rows have source_pages and cross_checked_by filled in.

Maps: Faden's 1777 map was rebuilt from the full scan at 7 m a pixel (it was 12) in four pieces; a new map row, faden-1777-sheet, is the engraving as printed, reached by the 1:1 button, with units placed on it by the same fit (Maps column xy_from). Routes taken (playback setting trails) draws the roads each unit has marched.
What changed on 18 November 2026: a source register

Sources are now kept as one register. The Sources sheet has nine new columns: kind (map, official report, book, article, website, dataset, marker, reference, official history, letter), war, rights_status, may_host (yes, yes with credit, check, or no: link and cite), rights_checked, site, local_copy (where the file is kept in the WarMapper folder), page_offset (for a scanned volume, how its PDF pages relate to the printed ones) and part_of (a report printed inside a volume). The values in kind, rights_status and may_host were worked out from the type and rights columns and are worth a check.

New source S62: the Official Records, Series I, Volume 27, Part 1, from the HathiTrust scan Morgan supplied (public domain); S01 to S03 are reports inside it. New sheet Source uses: one row per source and campaign, counting the position, event, route, unit and period-map rows that cite it (formulas, so the counts keep up; a 0 means none of those rows cite it, though it may be used on Battles, Places or Conflicts). New sheet Source candidates: sources found but not yet cited, each with a status (found, located, rights checked, read in part, read, in use, not useful): the American Revolution Institute map collection, The Statements of Time, and the reports of Doubleday, Wadsworth, Hancock and Howard. On Positions, two new columns: source_pages (the page each source gives for the row, such as "S62 p. 266") and cross_checked_by (the other sources that confirm the row).

Rules: a source whose may_host is not yes is linked and cited, never copied into the project. A candidate moves to Sources when the data first cites it. Each time or position is checked against at least one other authoritative source before it is accepted. Large scans stay in the WarMapper folder (local_copy), not in the code repository.
What changed on 17 November 2026 (later): Trenton checked against Elliott; Trenton and Ypres playbacks

Trenton was checked against The New Jersey Campaign, 1776-1777 by Steven E. Elliott (U.S. Army Center of Military History; source S59), the 1929 History of Trenton (S22, read again in full) and two Journal of the American Revolution articles (S60 on the crossing, S61 on the Hessians who escaped). 49 Trenton rows now say in the new column "check: Elliott (S59), S22 and JAR (S60, S61)" whether the sources agree. The v10 column on Conflicts adds what they say to TC01 to TC12, and TC13 to TC17 are new.

What the check changed in the data: the crossing now ends between 2 and 4 a.m. (TE03); the jäger picket reaches the bridge at 08:14, not 08:02; one event was added (the escape over the bridge); two Hessian commanders and nine American brigade strengths come from Elliott. No position was moved: where the books disagree (Stephen's brigade, where Rall fell) the rows keep the 1929 history and Stryker and the disagreement is a conflict.

Playbacks: at Trenton the army marches as Greene's and Sullivan's divisions, which part at Birmingham, and every brigade marches with its division from the ferry instead of appearing in the town; a Satellite map and a Formations view were added. At Ypres a unit that joins after the first day is drawn coming up, out of its corps or from behind its own lines, and a Formations view (corps) was added. On Tracks, start_route can now name several routes in order.
What changed on 17 November 2026: Gettysburg checked against Reardon and Vossler

Gettysburg only. The first day was checked against The Gettysburg Campaign, June-July 1863 by Carol Reardon and Tom Vossler (U.S. Army Center of Military History, 2013; source S55). 53 position rows now say in the new column "check: Reardon and Vossler (S55)" whether the booklet agrees, with the page. The Conflicts sheet has a new v9 column on nine conflicts and one new conflict (C13, the time of the railroad-cut fight). 23 unit commanders are now as printed in the booklet.

What the check changed in the data: Reynolds's death moved from 10:50 to a range of 10:15 to 10:50 and is shown before the railroad cut; four events hold wider time ranges; one event was added (the town taken, about 5 p.m.). No position was moved. Three differences need a ruling: the first shot (7:00 or 7:30), Archer on Herr Ridge (9:00 or 10:00), and the railroad cut (10:30 or towards noon). Coddington (S56) could not be read: see gap G22.
What changed on 15 November 2026: Gettysburg, the whole first day

Gettysburg only. The playback now runs from 7:15 a.m. to 5:30 p.m. 71 position rows (P39 to P109), 34 units, 25 tracks, 11 events (GE07 to GE17), 3 conflicts (C10 to C12) and 4 gaps (G18 to G21) are new. The brigades of the First and Eleventh Corps and of Heth's, Pender's, Rodes's and Early's divisions are entered; regiments and batteries after the morning are not.

Every new position with coordinate source map_read was read from Bachelder's first-day map (S18) and carries the time printed beside its bars. Where the map prints no time the time_basis column says so and says what the shown time rests on. The eleven evening rows on Cemetery Hill are estimates (G19). All new rows are marked Needs review.
What changed in v7

First Ypres only. The British and French lines are now read from the dated sketch maps of the British official history: the line drawn for 21, 23, 25, 29 and 31 October and for 4, 9 and 11 November. 74 Allied rows carry a line read from a sketch; each holds until the day before the next sketch. Rows between those dates that rest on text are still there and say so. Positions now has 215 Ypres rows (v6 had 143).

The sketches show German formations as arrows, not lines. German rows keep the places the German account names; where that put a German line on or behind the Allied line as now mapped, its points are moved 500 m clear and marked "derived" (37 rows). A row whose line had to change as the Allied line moved is split by date.

A row read from a sketch has its points in the lat, lon, via and line_end columns and no place_ids, because the points are not named places. Its place_description says which sketch and gives the ends of the line by the nearest village. The description used before v7 is kept in the notes.

Every changed or new row says what happened in the "changed in v7" column. A row that was split keeps its pos_id for the first part of its time. Four inferred French rows are withdrawn because the sketches contradict them: Y057 (18 Div (Fr), 11-10 to 11-22): An inferred French retreat towards Pilckem on 10 November. Sketch 14 shows the French line still running from the canal near Steenstraat past Kortekeer on the afternoon of the 11th.; Y058 (31 Div (Fr), 10-29 to 11-09): An inferred line from Steenstraat to Bixschoote. Sketch 9 puts the 31st Division near Poelcappelle on 29 October and "De Mitry" at Bixschoote.; Y059 (31 Div (Fr), 11-10 to 11-22): An inferred retreat to the canal on 10 November. Sketches 13 and 14 put "Vidal" south of Ypres, next to Cavan, on 9 and 11 November.; Y061 (32 Div (Fr), 11-10 to 11-22): An inferred loss of St. Eloi on 10 November, from the German account. Sketches 13 and 14 keep the French line about 1 km south-east of St. Eloi on 9 and 11 November (YC07).

What the sketches changed most, as I read them: they show no French retreat towards Pilckem on 10 November (YC12); they keep St. Eloi inside the French line on 11 November (YC07); they agree with the German account that Hill 60 was lost on the 11th (YC05); they still draw the British 1st Division in reserve on 25 October (YC11); and they put "Vidal" north of Ypres on 31 October and south of it by 9 November. These are readings of a printed sketch by eye against a kilometre grid, not of the text. Two French units are new (Hély d'Oissel's group; the Woillemont and Olleris detachments) and the French IX and XVI Corps now have rows of their own. Conflicts and Gaps have a "v7 update" column; YC11, YC12 and YG14 to YG17 are new.
What changed in v6

First Ypres only. The sketch maps bound into the British official history are now in hand. Sketch A, a contoured map of the Ypres area, is georeferenced and is a base map in the playback. Ten places that had been put in from memory, or that sit in a different spot on today's map, are now read from it; the rows that use them say so under "changed in v6". The dated sketches (18 October to 11 November) are in the playback as a backdrop but have not yet been used to correct the unit lines: that is the next step, and it will change many rows.
What changed in v5

First Ypres added: 215 position rows for 50 corps and divisions, 61 units in all, 69 assignment rows, 15 events, 12 conflicts and 17 gaps. Gettysburg and Trenton are as they were in v4: if you have reviewed rows in v4, send it back and I will merge your columns by pos_id.

This pilot is at a different scale. Time is in days, not minutes: a row runs from the evening of its first date to the evening of its last. A position is a sector, a line through named villages, not a point. Units are corps and divisions.

New sheet, Places: every village or feature a Ypres position uses, with its name in the 1914 sources, its name today, coordinates and how it was placed. Positions list their places in the new place_ids column. Battles has a new extent_km column so that the distance check fits the size of the battle.

Two new checks: K14 (the lines of opposing units must not cross) and K15 (every place named is on the Places sheet). The closeness check (K09) is not run for Ypres, because the two sides' lines are drawn apart by hand and the gap means nothing.

Coordinate confidence for Ypres is on a wider scale than for the other two battles: high within 500 m, medium within 1 km, low beyond. Almost every Ypres row is a line through village centres, so read the playback as a diagram, not a trench map.
One fix to older data: units with echelon "Army" now carry the symbol code for an army (23), not a blank echelon.
What changed in v4

Trenton only. Coordinates now come from the current street map (OpenStreetMap) and from Lt. Wiederhold's 1776 sketch, which Morgan supplied. 37 rows have new coordinates and 7 rows are new; the column "changed in v4" says what changed on each. Gettysburg is untouched.

The sketch settled where the Hessians formed, fought and surrendered: the three written descriptions of the surrender ground turn out to be one block of today's city (Conflicts, TC08). It also raised three new questions (TC10 to TC12).
What changed in v3

The data is now stored the way the full product would store it: one table per kind of thing, joined by IDs. A position is one record that points to a unit, a campaign, an optional battle and its sources. The nested view (war, battle, side, unit, location) is produced from these tables, not stored.
Gettysburg: all 38 rows carried over with your review status and notes unchanged. Units were split into Units (who they are) and Assignments (parent, commander and strength for a date range).
Trenton: 61 new position rows, 39 units, 11 routes, 12 conflicts and 11 gaps. (Row counts are as of v4.)
New fields

Times: each position has an earliest and latest start and an earliest and latest end, as "YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM", a date alone, or "unknown". Where sources disagree the two times differ. Gettysburg example: Archer's line starts between 9:00 (the map) and 9:30 (the reports).

coord_source: map_read (read off a georeferenced, surveyed period map), sketch_read (read off a period sketch and placed on the current map), modern_map (a named street corner or building on the current map), marker (a monument or marker at the spot), derived (worked out from other points), estimate (placed from a description), none. coord_precision_m is my estimate of how far off the point could be.
via: extra points along a line that bends. Routes: the path a unit took between two positions, as waypoints. Events and Phases: the chapter markers for playback.

symbol_code: the standard 20-digit military symbol code for each unit, so any mapping tool can draw it. wikidata_qid: the public ID that joins wars and battles to outside datasets. Units do not have them yet (gap G16).
Sheets and how they link

Wars > Campaigns > Battles (a battle can have a parent battle) > Phases. Sides belong to a war. Units belong to a side. Assignments give each unit its parent, commander and strength for a date range. Positions, Routes and Events point to a unit, a campaign and, where it applies, a battle. March and camp rows have no battle.
Conflicts, Gaps and Sources work as before, with a column saying which battle they belong to. Georeference covers both period maps.
Checks
15 rules are run over the data every time the file is built, and the findings are on the Checks sheet: 0 errors, 25 for review, 36 notes. 13 rules passed cleanly.
"Review" findings are not mistakes in the file; they are places where the data itself looks doubtful, such as two opposing units drawn in the same place.
How to review

On the Positions sheet set review_status (yellow) to Accepted, Corrected or Rejected and type corrections in reviewer_notes. A correction needs a source: a report, a tablet, a map or a book with a page. An AI or search summary on its own is not a source.

For Trenton and Ypres, wording that begins "Paraphrase:" is my summary of the source, not a quotation. Only text inside quotation marks is quoted. The Ypres quotations came through a reading tool and have not been checked against the page (gap YG07).
Counts: each war's own counts are now on the Read me sheet of its workbook.
This workbook is the master copy of the battle data (since 15 Nov 2026). The playbacks are written from it by tools/export_battles.py; nothing else feeds them.

New sheets: Playbacks (one row per playback), Playback settings (one setting per row), Tracks (one row per symbol on the map: which Positions rows it follows), Nations, Labels (names on the map), Maps (period maps and where they sit).

New columns, shaded green: Positions (show_from, show_to: when the playback draws the row; map_id, map_xy: its place on a map that is not to scale), Events (timeline, playback_at, playback_label, playback_text), Routes (playback), Sides (code, short).
The Checks sheet was written when the workbook was last generated (v7). It is not updated by hand edits; the export script runs its own checks and refuses to write a battle file that fails them.

Maps, columns iiif_...: where a library serves the full scan as zoomable tiles (the IIIF image service), so the playback can show full detail when the reader zooms in. iiif_region is the part of the scan the first picture shows (left, top, right, bottom, in scan pixels); iiif_reduced is how large that picture is against the scan.

19 Nov 2026: new sheet Summaries (one row per day or week of a playback: kind, from, to, title, text, source_ids). When a battle longer than two days stops at the end of a day or week, the text pane shows the matching summary. First Ypres has one for every day and every week, written only from its own Positions and Events rows.
